title: 3D Scaffolds with Nanohydroxyapatite for Chondrogenic Differentiation of Stem Cells
author: Talouki, Tackallou, et al.
materials: In this study, a series of nHA-nanocomposite scaffolds were fabricated using 100:0:0, 60:40:0, and 60:20:20 weight ratios of PGS to PCL: Gel copolymers through salt leaching method. The morphology and porosity of prepared samples was characterized by SEM and EDX mapping analysis. Also, the dynamic contact angle and PBS adsorption tests are used to identify the effect of copolymerization and nanoparticles on scaffolds' hydrophilicity. The hydrolytic degradation properties were also analyzed. Furthermore, cell viability and proliferation as well as cell adhesion are evaluated to find out the biocompatibility. To determine the potential ability of nHA-nanocomposite scaffolds in chondrogenic differentiation, RT-PCR assay was performed to monitor the expression of collagen II, aggrecan, and Sox9 genes as markers of cartilage differentiation.

Human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (h ADSCs) were supplied from the Iranian Biological Resource Center and cultured in a Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM; BIOSERA, USA)/F12 containing 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS; Gibco, USA), 100 U/mL penicillin and 100 µg/ml streptomycin (Invitrogen) at 37 °C and 5% CO2 in 95% humidity.hADSCs were cultured until reaching a confluence between 70 and 80%. The culture medium was changed every 3 days. Four groups of scaffolds including PGS, PGS/PCL/Gel, PGS/PCL/Gel/HA3%, and PGS/PCL/Gel/HA5% in three replicates were placed in 1 cm × 1 cm wells of 12-well plates in DMEM F-12 medium and fourth passage culture of cells (5 × 105 cells/cm2) was seeded on the scaffolds and cultured in the proliferation culture medium for desired times (1,7 and 14 days). The culture medium was changed every 3 days.

After in vitro cultivation for 21 days, total RNA was extracted from the cell-scaffold constructs using a standard TRIzol procedure (Kiazist, Iran), according to the manufacturer’s protocol, and the concentration and purity of the RNA were determined using a NanoDrop ND-2000 spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher, USA). The mRNA was reverse-transcribed into cDNA using an Easy cDNA Synthesis Kit (Parstous, Iran). The expression levels of genes encoding collagen II, aggrecan, Sox9, and Osteocalcin were quantified using RT-PCR on a Real-time PCR thermocycler (ABI Stepone, USA). steps.title: Dissolve copolymers in solvent
steps.instruction: Prepare polymer solutions by weighing the desired weight ratios of PGS, PCL, and gelatin (100:0:0, 60:40:0, and 60:20:20) and dissolve each mixture in a chloroform/HDI (4:1 v/v) solvent system to a final concentration of 10 % w/v; stir overnight.

steps.title: Add HA nanoparticles and catalyst
steps.instruction: To each polymer solution add hydroxyapatite (HA) nanoparticles at 3 % or 5 % w.t. (for the nanocomposite formulations) and then add 1,4‑tin octanoate catalyst to a final concentration of 10 ppm; mix for 30 min until homogeneous.

steps.title: Incorporate salt and cast scaffolds
steps.instruction: Add a specific amount of NaCl particles (size > 100 µm) to each polymer‑nanoparticle mixture, stir briefly, then pour the slurry into a mold of appropriate size.

steps.title: Dry and leach salt from scaffolds
steps.instruction: Allow the cast samples to dry completely in the mold, demold them, and immerse the dried scaffolds in distilled water for 7 days, changing the water as needed to fully remove the salt.

steps.title: Culture hADSCs to confluence
steps.instruction: Thaw human adipose‑derived mesenchymal stem cells (hADSCs) and expand them in DMEM/F12 (BIOSERA, USA) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Gibco, USA), 100 U mL⁻¹ penicillin and 100 µg mL⁻¹ streptomycin (Invitrogen) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 95 % humidity; passage cells until they reach 70–80 % confluence, changing medium every 3 days.

steps.title: Pre‑wet scaffolds before seeding
steps.instruction: Place each dried scaffold (1 cm × 1 cm) into a well of a 12‑well plate, add a small volume of the same culture medium, and incubate overnight in a BINDER (Germany) incubator to improve cell attachment.

steps.title: Seed hADSCs onto scaffolds
steps.instruction: Using fourth‑passage hADSCs, seed 5 × 10⁵ cells cm⁻² (approximately 5 × 10⁵ cells per scaffold) onto the pre‑wetted scaffolds placed in 12‑well plates (three replicates per formulation: PGS, PGS/PCL/Gel, PGS/PCL/Gel/HA 3 %, PGS/PCL/Gel/HA 5 %).

steps.title: Maintain cultures and change medium
steps.instruction: Incubate the cell‑scaffold constructs at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, 95 % humidity and change the proliferation medium every 3 days; culture for the desired time points (1, 7, and 14 days).

steps.title: Extract total RNA from constructs
steps.instruction: After 21 days of in‑vitro culture, lyse each cell‑scaffold construct with TRIzol reagent (Kiazist, Iran) following the manufacturer’s protocol, isolate total RNA, and measure concentration and purity using a NanoDrop ND‑2000 spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher, USA).

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA from RNA
steps.instruction: Reverse‑transcribe the extracted RNA into cDNA using the Easy cDNA Synthesis Kit (Parstous, Iran) according to the kit instructions.

steps.title: Set up SYBR Green real‑time PCR
steps.instruction: Prepare PCR reactions with SYBR Green Master Mix (2 ×, high ROX, Addbio, Korea), gene‑specific primers (collagen II, aggrecan, Sox9, Osteocalcin, GAPDH; sequences from Sinaclon, Iran), and cDNA template; load reactions onto an ABI StepOne real‑time PCR thermocycler (USA).

substeps.instruction: 40 cycles of: 95 °C for 15 s (denaturation), 60 °C for 15–20 s (annealing), 72 °C for 30 s (extension).

steps.title: Run PCR and analyze gene expression
steps.instruction: Perform each sample in triplicate, normalize target gene Ct values to GAPDH, and calculate relative expression of collagen II, aggrecan, Sox9, and Osteocalcin to assess chondrogenic differentiation.
